business_patterns.top_pattern: VA DSNP acute hospital admissions are the dominant cost driver
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: VA DSNP HMO acute hospital inpatient spend with prior authorization
business_patterns.pattern_details: VA DSNP HMO acute hospital spend increased sharply, and the increase is predominantly an admission-growth story rather than a pricing story. Volume rose across major hospitals, while paid and allowed per admission declined, indicating that more inpatient use is overwhelming modest unit-cost relief. The pattern is concentrated enough to support immediate hospital- and market-level action.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This is the single largest identified driver, so reducing avoidable inpatient use in this market has the biggest near-term savings potential.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Launch a VA DSNP inpatient action plan with the top hospitals focused on admission appropriateness, readmissions, discharge planning, and care-transition controls for prior-authorized acute stays.
evidence_summary: VA DSNP HMO acute hospital spend rose about $58.9M.
The increase was driven by about 3,445 more admissions and 3,759 more claims, while paid per admit fell about $467.
The largest visible provider concentrations were VCU Medical Center, Sentara Norfolk General Hospital, and Sentara Leigh Hospital, contributing about $9.9M combined.

business_patterns.top_pattern: TX authorization-code movement must be validated before business action
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: TX authorization classification and prior-authorization coding
business_patterns.pattern_details: TX shows a large shift in authorization-code assignment that can make utilization or reimbursement changes appear larger than they really are. This is a gating validation issue, not a confirmed medical-cost trend. Business action on policy, provider performance, or utilization should wait until the auth-code movement is reconciled.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: If this shift is not corrected first, subsequent provider, UM, and reimbursement actions may target the wrong problem.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Audit the TX auth-to-claim mapping and code assignment logic, then restate the affected claims before pursuing provider or utilization interventions.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The group is explicitly flagged for auth or mapping shift and requires validation before action.
evidence_summary: TX auth-code movement carries about $35.8M of apparent impact and is flagged for validation before action.
The visible provider concentration is Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital, but the core issue is the authorization-code shift itself.
Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital shows only about a $129K offset beneath the broader TX auth-code movement.

business_patterns.top_pattern: TX DSNP acute hospital growth is a broad utilization surge
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital inpatient spend with prior authorization
business_patterns.pattern_details: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend rose materially on top of significant admission growth. Unlike VA, this market also shows some upward paid-per-admission movement, so the issue is not purely volume. The broad market signal supports a combined utilization and reimbursement review, with utilization still the main lever.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A market-wide inpatient increase of this size can quickly compound if admissions and per-admit costs both continue rising.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Run a TX DSNP acute inpatient deep dive to identify the admission sources and service lines driving the increase, then tighten prior-authorization and concurrent-review workflows for the highest-growth hospital stays.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend increased about $35.4M.
Growth came with about 1,671 more admissions and 1,968 more claims.
Paid per admit increased about $455, adding mild unit-cost pressure on top of utilization growth.

business_patterns.top_pattern: Memorial Hermann Southwest is a concentrated TX provider-cost hotspot across Medicare products
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: TX acute hospital spend concentrated at Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital
business_patterns.pattern_details: A meaningful share of TX acute-hospital pressure is concentrated at Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital across several Medicare products. Both admissions and paid per admit increased, with the largest exposure in DSNP HMO and Medicare HMO. This is a focused provider economics issue with a clear target for contract, pricing, and care-management intervention.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: A single-provider concentration creates a practical opportunity to address cost trend through network, reimbursement, and UM levers rather than only broad market actions.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Perform a provider-specific review at Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital covering contract terms, claim pricing, admission mix, and prior-authorization performance across DSNP HMO first, then Medicare HMO, CSNP HMO, and SNP Crossover.
evidence_summary: Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital drove about $6.6M in TX DSNP HMO acute hospital pressure with 332 more admissions and about $8.0K higher paid per admit.
The same provider added about $3.3M in Medicare HMO acute hospital spend with 153 more admissions and about $4.8K higher paid per admit.
Smaller but consistent increases also appeared in CSNP HMO (+$349K) and SNP Crossover (+$341K).

business_patterns.top_pattern: VA SNP spending is shifting into SNF, rehab, and acute psych settings
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: VA DSNP HMO and CSNP HMO post-acute and behavioral facility mix
business_patterns.pattern_details: VA SNP growth is not limited to acute hospitals; spending is also moving into SNF, physical rehab, and acute psych settings. SNF and acute psych show both higher volume and higher per-admission cost, while physical rehab is mainly a volume story. This points to site-of-care management opportunities across discharge planning, level-of-care decisions, and preferred post-acute pathways.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: Post-acute and behavioral site-of-care leakage can sustain medical-cost trend even if acute inpatient growth slows.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Tighten VA post-acute referral steering and level-of-care review for SNF, rehab, and acute psych admissions, with special focus on DSNP HMO SNF pathways and discharge practices from acute hospitals.
evidence_summary: VA DSNP HMO SNF spend rose about $8.6M with about 911 more admissions and about $2.1K higher paid per admit.
VA DSNP HMO Physical Rehab added about $1.9M on 76 more admissions even as paid per admit fell about $4.2K.
VA DSNP HMO Acute Psych added about $1.8M with 176 more admissions and about $2.5K higher paid per admit.
VA CSNP HMO SNF added about $982K with 122 more admissions.

business_patterns.top_pattern: VA CSNP acute hospital growth is broad, with added provider-level cost pressure
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: VA CSNP HMO acute hospital inpatient spend with prior authorization
business_patterns.pattern_details: VA CSNP acute hospital spend increased through a combination of broader admission growth and added provider-level cost pressure. The broad market signal shows more inpatient use, while specific hospitals show higher paid per admit. The action should combine admission management with targeted hospital performance review.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This extends the VA inpatient pressure beyond DSNP and suggests a wider SNP hospital-management issue in the market.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Expand the VA inpatient response beyond DSNP by reviewing CSNP admission drivers and hospital-specific pricing or severity patterns at VCU, Riverside, Sentara Leigh, and Sentara Norfolk.
evidence_summary: VA CSNP HMO acute hospital signals total about $8.4M.
Broad utilization added about $6.5M with 481 more admissions while paid per admit fell about $2.3K.
Separate provider-level pressure at Sentara Leigh Hospital and Sentara Norfolk General Hospital added about $1.9M with higher paid per admit.

business_patterns.top_pattern: CA / VA / WI also show authorization-code shifts that can distort performance readings
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: CA / VA / WI authorization classification and prior-authorization coding
business_patterns.pattern_details: A separate multistate authorization-code movement is present across CA, VA, and WI and should be treated as another gating validation issue. The clearest visible concentration is in VA hospitals, but the scope spans all three listed states. Until the auth-code assignment is validated, provider and utilization conclusions in these markets remain at risk of misclassification.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: This issue can contaminate downstream provider, UM, and reimbursement decisions across multiple markets if left unresolved.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Validate the authorization-code crosswalk and assignment process for CA, VA, and WI, then rerun provider and utilization views on the corrected claims set.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The group is explicitly flagged for auth or mapping shift and requires validation before action.
evidence_summary: A multistate auth-code shift across CA, VA, and WI carries about $5.6M of apparent impact and is flagged for validation before action.
VA is the clearest visible concentration, including about $2.2M at the state level.
Within VA, VCU Medical Center and Sentara Leigh Hospital together account for about $2.0M of the shifted amount.

business_patterns.top_pattern: TX Not Mapped facility growth is a second gating validation issue
business_patterns.what_is_impacting: TX DSNP HMO claims classified to Not Mapped facility type
business_patterns.pattern_details: TX has a large increase in claims assigned to a Not Mapped facility category, and the size of the per-admission increase is too large to treat as a routine utilization change without validation. This could reflect misclassification of site of care, provider setup issues, or other mapping defects. Validate the facility assignment first, then decide whether any utilization or reimbursement action is warranted.
business_patterns.why_it_matters: An unmapped facility bucket of this size can hide the true site of care and send teams to the wrong operational lever.
business_patterns.recommended_next_step: Correct the TX facility mapping for Not Mapped claims and reclassify the affected spend before escalating to provider contracting, site-of-care, or prior-authorization policy changes.
business_patterns.validation_reason: The main driver sits in an unmapped facility bucket, so classification must be validated before interpreting it as a real care-pattern change.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO claims in the Not Mapped facility bucket increased about $8.3M.
The bucket shows about 201 more admissions and an extremely large paid-per-admit increase of about $29.1K.
Because the facility type is unmapped, utilization, reimbursement, and site-of-care conclusions should wait until classification is corrected.

executive_summary.headline: The main story is large SNP inpatient growth in VA and TX, paired with separate authorization-code and facility-mapping issues that must be cleaned up before some provider actions are taken.
executive_summary.primary_business_message: VA DSNP HMO acute hospital utilization is the biggest confirmed cost driver, while TX shows both broad DSNP acute-hospital growth and concentrated provider pressure at Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital. At the same time, TX and CA / VA / WI contain material authorization-code shifts, and TX also has a large Not Mapped facility bucket, so part of the observed change is a validation problem that should be resolved before policy or network action.
recommended_focus_order: Validate TX authorization-code distribution and Not Mapped facility classification before taking provider or UM action on those claims.
Address confirmed acute-hospital growth in VA DSNP HMO and TX DSNP HMO, starting with admission management and care-transition controls.
Target concentrated provider and site-of-care pressure next, especially Memorial Hermann Southwest Hospital in TX and SNF / rehab / acute psych pathways in VA.

notes: Synthesis intentionally prioritized the highest-impact authorization, provider mix, inpatient utilization, and site-of-care themes requested for business leaders.
Clinical-only case-mix groups and lower-dollar small-volume operational groups were left ungrouped to keep the table focused on actionable authorization and provider mix patterns.

Some sizable VA Not Mapped groups remain ungrouped because the final table favored the larger TX unmapped pattern and the explicit multistate authorization-code validation issue within the 8-pattern limit.
Left 41 analytical groups unassigned to preserve clean narrative attribution.
Segment attribution is weak for 29% of cards (40 of 140) on segment_by [service_area_state]; add those dimensions to the stage's dimension or carry-through list to attribute them at cell level.
